question: Kumbh Mela and Sangam are famous in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sangam at Prayagraj (Allahabad), Uttar Pradesh, is the confluence of three rivers — Ganga, Yamuna and the mythical Saraswati — and is one of the four sites where the Kumbh Mela is held. (संगम, प्रयागराज — उत्तर प्रदेश)

 

• The Kumbh Mela is one of the largest peaceful religious gatherings in the world, held once every 12 years at each of the four sites, with an Ardh (half) Kumbh every 6 years at Haridwar and Prayagraj.

 

• The Prayagraj Kumbh Mela was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2017.

 

• The festival involves a ritual bath (Shahi Snan) by pilgrims and various akharas of sadhus at the sacred confluence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The four Kumbh Mela sites are Prayagraj (Uttar Pradesh) on the Ganga-Yamuna-Saraswati Sangam, Haridwar (Uttarakhand) on the Ganga, Ujjain (Madhya Pradesh) on the Shipra, and Nashik (Maharashtra) on the Godavari.

 

• The rotation among these four sites follows the movement of Jupiter, the Sun and the Moon into specific zodiac signs, per Hindu astrology.

 

NOTE

 

• Meghalaya (Option 1), Manipur (Option 3) and Sikkim (Option 4): These are north-eastern states and are not among the four traditional Kumbh Mela/Sangam sites.

question: The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, which provides for the more effective prevention of certain unlawful activities of individuals and associations dealing with terrorist activities, was first put into effect in India in the year:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1967.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) was enacted in 1967 to make provision for the more effective prevention of certain unlawful activities of individuals and associations, and for dealing with terrorist activities. (गैरकानूनी गतिविधियां (रोकथाम) अधिनियम — 1967)

 

• It empowers the central government to declare an association as "unlawful" and, after later amendments, to designate an individual as a terrorist.

 

• The Act has since been amended several times — notably in 2004, 2008, 2012 and 2019 — to strengthen anti-terror provisions, including the 2019 amendment allowing individuals (not just organisations) to be designated terrorists.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The National Investigation Agency (NIA), set up in 2009, is the primary agency that investigates offences under the UAPA.

 

• Bodies once banned under UAPA include organisations such as SIMI and various insurgent/terrorist outfits.

 

NOTE

 

• 1991, 2014 and 1947 (Options 1, 3 and 4): None of these mark the enactment of the UAPA; the Act was first put into effect in 1967, well before and well after these years respectively.

question: In 11th century, the army of which of the following Cholas reached upto Ganga to invade Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajendra I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rajendra I (Rajendra Chola I), son of Rajaraja I, sent his army on a famous expedition to the Gangetic plains around 1019-1023 CE, defeating the Pala ruler Mahipala I of Bengal/Bihar. (राजेंद्र प्रथम — गंगा अभियान)

 

• To commemorate this victory, Rajendra I assumed the title "Gangaikonda Chola" (bringer of the Ganga) and built a new capital, Gangaikondacholapuram, with a great Shiva temple there.

 

• He is also credited with a naval expedition against the Srivijaya empire of Southeast Asia, making the Cholas a dominant maritime power.

 

• This Ganga expedition took place in the early 11th century, matching the question's timeframe.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rajaraja I, Rajendra's father, built the Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur and conquered Sri Lanka and the Maldives.

 

• Vijayalaya founded the imperial Chola line in the 9th century by capturing Thanjavur from the Muttaraiyars.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajaraja I (Option 2): Known for naval conquests and the Thanjavur temple, not the Ganga expedition.

 

• Vijayalaya (Option 3): The founder of the Chola dynasty's imperial line (9th century), too early for this expedition.

 

• Rajadhiraj I (Option 4): Successor of Rajendra I; known for wars against the Chalukyas, not the Ganga campaign.

question: Which of the following is used in solar cookers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mirror.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A solar cooker uses a mirror (reflector), usually a concave or plane mirror, to reflect and concentrate sunlight onto the cooking vessel, converting solar radiation into heat. (सौर कुकर — दर्पण/परावर्तक)

 

• A box-type solar cooker has an insulated box with a glass top and an adjustable plane mirror as a reflector, while a parabolic/concentrator-type solar cooker uses a concave mirror to focus sunlight to a point for higher temperatures.

 

• The blackened interior/tray absorbs the concentrated solar radiation and converts it into heat, cooking the food without any external electrical or fuel supply.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Solar cookers are a form of renewable, non-polluting energy device and are widely promoted under India's solar energy and rural energy programmes.

 

• The greenhouse effect inside the glass-covered box also helps trap heat, raising the internal temperature further.

 

NOTE

 

• Electrical supply (Option 1) and Electrochemical cell (Option 4): Solar cookers work purely on reflected sunlight and need no electrical or battery input.

 

• Solar plate (Option 2): Not the functional component of a solar cooker; solar (photovoltaic) plates convert sunlight to electricity, which is a different technology (solar panels), not solar cookers.

question: According to Census of India 2011, what is the percentage of the rural population of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 68.8%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, about 68.84% (approximately 68.8%) of India's population lived in rural areas, while roughly 31.16% lived in urban areas. (जनगणना 2011 — ग्रामीण जनसंख्या 68.8%)

 

• India's total population as per Census 2011 was about 121.09 crore, of which around 83.3 crore were classified as rural and 37.7 crore as urban.

 

• The rural-urban split is defined by Census criteria such as presence of a municipality/corporation, minimum population and non-agricultural workforce share for a settlement to be classified as urban.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2011 Census was the 15th Census of India and the 7th after Independence; its motto was "Our Census, Our Future".

 

• Uttar Pradesh was the most populous state, and the rural share of population has been gradually declining Census after Census due to urbanisation.

 

NOTE

 

• 65.25%, 70% and 69% (Options 1, 2 and 3): These do not match the actual Census 2011 figure of approximately 68.8% for the rural population share.

question: Article 51 A of the Indian Constitution came in to effect from _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3rd January 1977.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 51A, which lays down the Fundamental Duties of citizens under Part IVA of the Constitution, was inserted by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, and came into effect from 3 January 1977. (मूल कर्तव्य, अनुच्छेद 51A — 3 जनवरी 1977)

 

• This provision was added on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, drawing inspiration from the Fundamental Duties listed in the erstwhile USSR's Constitution.

 

• Originally, Article 51A listed 10 Fundamental Duties; an 11th duty (regarding parents providing education to children aged 6-14) was added later by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 is often called the "Mini-Constitution" because of the sweeping changes it made, including adding the words "Socialist", "Secular" and "Integrity" to the Preamble.

 

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, i.e., they are not enforceable by courts, unlike Fundamental Rights.

 

NOTE

 

• 5th March 1978, 11th March 1980 and 10th March 1979 (Options 1, 2 and 4): None of these correspond to the actual date on which the 42nd Amendment's Fundamental Duties provision came into force, which was 3 January 1977.

question: The 'Karma' tribal dance form is associated with which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Karma dance is a popular tribal folk dance of Chhattisgarh, performed by tribes such as the Gond, Baiga and Oraon to worship Karam Devta, the deity/tree of fate and good fortune, for a good harvest. (करमा नृत्य — छत्तीसगढ़)

 

• It is performed on Karma Ekadashi (Karma Puja), typically during the monsoon season, with men and women dancing together in circles to the beat of drums like the mandar and dhol.

 

• The dance is also performed in parts of neighbouring tribal belts of Jharkhand, Odisha and Madhya Pradesh, but it is most closely and traditionally identified with Chhattisgarh's tribal culture.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known folk dances of Chhattisgarh include Panthi, Raut Nacha and Saila.

 

• Chhattisgarh is home to numerous tribal communities and is often called the "rice bowl of India" alongside its rich tribal heritage.

 

NOTE

 

• Goa (Option 2): Known for dances like Dekhni and Fugdi, not Karma.

 

• Kerala (Option 3): Known for classical/folk forms like Kathakali, Theyyam and Mohiniyattam, not Karma.

 

• Karnataka (Option 4): Known for dances like Yakshagana and Dollu Kunitha, not Karma.

question: Who among the following is a figure in Indian music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Asha Bhosle.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Asha Bhosle is one of the most celebrated playback singers in Indian music, with a career spanning decades and thousands of songs across Hindi and regional cinema. (आशा भोसले — पार्श्व गायिका)

 

• She is the younger sister of legendary singer Lata Mangeshkar and has been honoured with the Padma Vibhushan, Bharat Ratna Dadasaheb Phalke Award, and multiple National Film Awards.

 

• She holds a Guinness World Record for being one of the most recorded artists in music history.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vyjayanthimala and Asha Parekh are noted actresses and dancers, not primarily musicians/singers.

 

• Amrita Pritam was a celebrated Punjabi poet and novelist, not a musician.

 

NOTE

 

• Vyjayanthi mala (Option 1): A well-known classical Bharatanatyam dancer and film actress, not a music figure.

 

• Amrita Pritam (Option 3): A renowned writer and poet, associated with literature, not music.

 

• Asha Parekh (Option 4): A veteran Bollywood actress, not a musician.

question:
Which of the following statements is true?

A) Money Supply is a stock concept

B) Currency and Coins with public are not included in M3 measure of money supply
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement A is correct: Money supply is a stock concept, i.e., it is measured at a specific point in time (like the last Friday of a fortnight), unlike a flow concept, which is measured over a period. (मुद्रा आपूर्ति — स्टॉक अवधारणा)

 

• Statement B is incorrect: Currency and coins held by the public ARE included in money supply. They form part of M1 (= currency with public + demand deposits with banks + other deposits with RBI), and since M3 = M1 + time deposits with banks, currency and coins with the public are very much a part of M3 as well.

 

• Therefore, only Statement A is true, while Statement B is factually wrong.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The RBI publishes four measures of money supply: M1, M2, M3 and M4, in decreasing order of liquidity, with M3 ("broad money") being the most widely used aggregate for policy analysis.

 

• M4 = M3 + total deposits with post office savings organisations (excluding National Savings Certificates).

 

NOTE

 

• Neither A nor B / Both A and B / Only B (Options 2, 3 and 4): These are incorrect because Statement A is true while Statement B is false, so the correct combination is "Only A" and none of these other combinations reflect that.

question: Hema Malini, a popular dancer and actress, received the ________ in 2000.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padma Shri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hema Malini, veteran Bollywood actress and trained Bharatanatyam dancer, was conferred the Padma Shri, India's fourth-highest civilian award, in the year 2000. (हेमा मालिनी — पद्म श्री 2000)

 

• She later went on to receive the Padma Bhushan (India's third-highest civilian award) in 2012, in recognition of her contributions to art and public life.

 

• Besides acting, she is a well-known classical dancer and has also served as a Member of Parliament from Mathura.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hema Malini is popularly known as the "Dream Girl" of Indian cinema, a title derived from her 1977 film of the same name.

 

• She has performed classical dance productions internationally and has trained under renowned gurus in Bharatanatyam.

 

NOTE

 

• Kabir Samman and Kalidas Samman (Options 2 and 4): These are state-level awards (Madhya Pradesh government honours for literature/music and performing arts respectively) not conferred on Hema Malini in 2000.

 

• Padma Vibhushan (Option 3): A higher civilian award than what she received in 2000; she has not been awarded the Padma Vibhushan.

question: What kind of smell do Esters have?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sweet smell like fruits.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Esters are organic compounds formed by the reaction of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol (esterification), and they characteristically have a sweet, fruity smell. (एस्टर — फलों जैसी मीठी गंध)

 

• Because of this pleasant fragrance, esters are widely used in the food and beverage industry as artificial flavouring agents (e.g., ethyl butyrate smells like pineapple, and octyl acetate smells like oranges) and in the perfume and cosmetics industry.

 

• Esters are also used as solvents and in the manufacture of plastics, soaps and polyesters.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) gas is what is responsible for the rotten egg smell, commonly associated with decayed organic matter.

 

• The general reaction is: Carboxylic acid + Alcohol → Ester + Water, catalysed by an acid (esterification reaction).

 

NOTE

 

• Rotten egg smell (Option 2): Characteristic of hydrogen sulfide, not esters.

 

• Floral smell (Option 3): More associated with natural flower fragrances/certain terpenes, not the defining odour of esters.

 

• Pungent smell (Option 4): More typical of acids like acetic acid/ammonia, opposite in character to the sweet smell of esters.

question: What is the name of the thermionic electron tube used to oscillate and amplify microwave frequency signals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Klystron.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Klystron is a specialised thermionic vacuum (electron) tube that works on the principle of velocity modulation of an electron beam and is used to both generate (oscillate) and amplify microwave-frequency signals. (क्लिस्ट्रॉन — माइक्रोवेव सिग्नल दोलन/प्रवर्धन)

 

• A reflex klystron is commonly used as a low-power microwave oscillator, while a multi-cavity (two-cavity) klystron is used as a high-power amplifier, e.g., in radar transmitters, satellite communication links and particle accelerators.

 

• Klystrons work by bunching electrons in velocity-modulated beams passing through resonant cavities, converting the kinetic energy of the beam into microwave energy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other microwave devices include the magnetron (used mainly as an oscillator, e.g. in microwave ovens and radar) and the Travelling Wave Tube (TWT) (a broadband amplifier).

 

• Klystrons find major applications in linear particle accelerators, TV transmitters and deep-space communication.

 

NOTE

 

• Neutrino (Option 1): Not a device at all — it is a fundamental subatomic particle with negligible mass and charge.

 

• Beam tetrodes (Option 2): A type of vacuum tube used in audio/power amplification, not specifically designed for microwave oscillation/amplification.

 

• Thyratron (Option 4): A gas-filled tube used as a high-power electrical switch, not for generating/amplifying microwave signals.

question: The Barren island is situated in the ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andaman Sea.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Barren Island is located in the Andaman Sea, part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands union territory of India, and is home to South Asia's only confirmed active volcano. (बैरन द्वीप — अंडमान सागर)

 

• The volcano on Barren Island has erupted several times in recent decades, including notable eruptions in 1991, 1994-95, 2005-06, and more recently in 2017 and 2022.

 

• The island lies about 138 km north-east of Port Blair and is uninhabited except for some flora/fauna adapted to volcanic terrain.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Andaman Sea is a part of the Indian Ocean/Bay of Bengal region, bounded by the Andaman and Nicobar Islands to the west and Myanmar/Thailand to the east.

 

• India's Andaman and Nicobar Islands also host Narcondam, a dormant volcano, distinct from the active Barren Island volcano.

 

NOTE

 

• Gulf of Mannar (Option 2): Located between Tamil Nadu (India) and Sri Lanka, far from Barren Island.

 

• Arabian Sea (Option 3): Lies on the western coast of India, unrelated to the Andaman Islands.

 

• Bay of Bengal (Option 4): While the Andaman Sea is sometimes loosely grouped with the wider Bay of Bengal region, Barren Island is specifically situated in the Andaman Sea, its own distinct marginal sea.

question: At the time of Independence of India, the Industrial sector was confined to ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is cotton textiles and jute.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the time of Independence in 1947, India's industrial base was narrow and largely confined to just two industries: cotton textiles and jute. (स्वतंत्रता के समय — सूती वस्त्र एवं जूट उद्योग)

 

• The cotton textile industry was concentrated mainly around Bombay (Mumbai) and Ahmedabad, while the jute industry was concentrated in and around Kolkata (Bengal), owing to easy access to raw jute grown in that region.

 

• Heavy and capital goods industries (steel, machinery, chemicals) were almost non-existent, reflecting the colonial policy of using India mainly as a source of raw materials and a market for British manufactured goods.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Post-independence, India's Industrial Policy Resolutions of 1948 and 1956, along with the Second Five-Year Plan (Mahalanobis model), focused on building a diversified industrial base, especially in the public sector heavy industries.

 

• The first modern cotton textile mill in India was set up in Mumbai in 1854, and the first jute mill near Kolkata in 1855.

 

NOTE

 

• jute and fertilizers (Option 1) and cotton textiles and fertilizers (Option 4): Fertilizer manufacturing was not a significant industry at the time of Independence.

 

• sugar and oil (Option 2): These were not the dominant/confining industries at Independence; cotton textiles and jute were the primary organised industries.

question: NDP at FC plus net factor income from abroad is equal to ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is NNP at FC.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• By definition of national income accounting: NNP at FC = NDP at FC + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA). (NDP at FC + NFIA = NNP at FC — राष्ट्रीय आय)

 

• NNP at Factor Cost (FC) is also known as National Income, and it represents the sum of factor incomes (rent, wages, interest, profit) earned by normal residents of a country, both domestically and abroad, net of depreciation.

 

• The general rule linking domestic and national aggregates is: National aggregate = Domestic aggregate + Net Factor Income from Abroad, which applies uniformly whether measured at market price or factor cost, and whether gross or net.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• NNP at FC (National Income) = NNP at MP - Net Indirect Taxes (Indirect Taxes - Subsidies).

 

• GDP at FC = GDP at MP - Net Indirect Taxes, and GNP at MP = GDP at MP + NFIA.

 

NOTE

 

• NNP at MP (Option 1): This equals NDP at MP + NFIA (market price basis), not factor cost basis as asked here.

 

• GDP at FC (Option 3): This is a purely domestic aggregate (NDP at FC + Depreciation), and does not involve net factor income from abroad.

 

• GNP at MP (Option 4): This equals GDP at MP + NFIA — a gross, market-price aggregate, not the net, factor-cost aggregate described in the question.

question: Who was appointed as the New Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is BVR Subrahmanyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• BVR Subrahmanyam, a 1987-batch IAS officer and former Union Commerce Secretary, was appointed as the CEO of NITI Aayog in February 2023, succeeding Parameswaran Iyer. (बी.वी.आर. सुब्रमण्यम — नीति आयोग सीईओ, 2023)

 

• As CEO, he heads the day-to-day administration and secretariat functions of NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India), the government's premier policy think tank, chaired by the Prime Minister.

 

• Before this role, he had earlier served as Chief Secretary of Jammu and Kashmir and held several key central government positions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015 and works as the government's premier policy think tank.

 

• Rajiv Kumar and Amitabh Kant are former Vice-Chairman and former CEO of NITI Aayog respectively, both prior to BVR Subrahmanyam's tenure.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajiv Kumar (Option 2): Former Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog, a different (and senior) post from CEO.

 

• Amitabh Kant (Option 3): Was CEO of NITI Aayog before Parameswaran Iyer, having completed his tenure prior to 2023.

 

• Parameswaran Iyer (Option 4): Was the CEO of NITI Aayog immediately before BVR Subrahmanyam, not the one appointed new CEO in 2023.

question: Which of the following teams won the Ranji Trophy 2022-23?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Saurashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Saurashtra won the Ranji Trophy 2022-23, defeating Bengal in the final, to lift their second Ranji Trophy title (their first title was in 2019-20). (रणजी ट्रॉफी 2022-23 — सौराष्ट्र विजेता)

 

• Pacer Jaydev Unadkat, Saurashtra's captain, led the side and played a key role with both bat and ball during the tournament.

 

• The Ranji Trophy is India's premier domestic first-class cricket championship, organised by the BCCI, contested among teams representing different states/regions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mumbai holds the record for the most Ranji Trophy titles (41+), by far the most successful team historically.

 

• The Ranji Trophy is named after Ranjitsinhji, a former Indian cricketer who played for England.

 

NOTE

 

• Bengal (Option 4): Bengal was the runner-up, losing to Saurashtra in the 2022-23 final.

 

• Hyderabad and Kerala (Options 2 and 3): Neither team reached the final of the Ranji Trophy 2022-23; Saurashtra and Bengal contested the final.

question: Which of the following crops is classified as fine grain?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wheat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Cereal crops are broadly classified into fine cereals/grains and coarse cereals/grains. Wheat (along with rice) is classified as a fine grain (cereal). (गेहूं — महीन अनाज)

 

• Coarse cereals (millets) include crops like bajra (pearl millet), ragi (finger millet), jowar (sorghum) and maize, which are generally hardier, more drought-resistant crops grown in less fertile/rain-fed regions.

 

• Wheat is one of India's two major staple food grains (with rice), grown predominantly in the Rabi season across states like Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana and Madhya Pradesh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India observes 2023 as the International Year of Millets, promoting coarse cereals like bajra, ragi and jowar for their nutritional and climate-resilience benefits (branded as "Shree Anna").

 

• The Green Revolution in India (from the mid-1960s) was primarily centred on high-yielding varieties of wheat and rice, the two main fine cereals.

 

NOTE

 

• Bajra (Option 1), Ragi (Option 2) and Maize (Option 3): All three are classified as coarse cereals (millets), not fine grains.

question: Who among the following Peshwas signed the Treaty of Bassein with the British East India Company?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Baji Rao II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Treaty of Bassein (1802) was signed between the Peshwa Baji Rao II and the British East India Company, under Governor-General Lord Wellesley. (बेसिन की संधि, 1802 — बाजी राव द्वितीय)

 

• Through this treaty, Baji Rao II accepted the Subsidiary Alliance, agreeing to maintain a British subsidiary force in his territory in exchange for British help against his Maratha rivals, effectively surrendering Maratha sovereignty.

 

• This treaty is regarded as a major turning point that led to the Second Anglo-Maratha War (1803-05) and marked the beginning of the end of Maratha independence.

 

• Baji Rao II was the last Peshwa of the Maratha Empire, finally defeated by the British in the Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817-18).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Subsidiary Alliance system was devised by Lord Wellesley and was also accepted by rulers of Hyderabad, Awadh, Mysore and other states.

 

• After his final defeat in 1818, Baji Rao II was pensioned off and settled at Bithoor, near Kanpur.

 

NOTE

 

• Madhav Rao (Option 2): A capable Peshwa (1761-1772) who restored Maratha power after the Third Battle of Panipat, well before the Treaty of Bassein.

 

• Narayan Rao (Option 3): A short-lived Peshwa (1772-73), assassinated in a Maratha court conspiracy, long before 1802.

 

• Balaji Baji Rao (Option 4): Peshwa during the Third Battle of Panipat (1761), decades before the Treaty of Bassein.

question: It is possible to derive the value of GDP of a country. Which function of money is applicable here?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Unit of account.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Money's function as a "unit of account" means it serves as a common measure of value, allowing the worth of vastly different goods and services to be expressed in the same monetary units and added up. (मुद्रा — लेखा की इकाई कार्य)

 

• GDP (Gross Domestic Product) is calculated by valuing all final goods and services produced within a country in monetary terms and summing them up — this aggregation is possible only because money acts as a common unit of account.

 

• Without a common unit of account, it would be impossible to compare or add together the value of, say, tonnes of steel and litres of milk into one aggregate figure like GDP.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The four primary functions of money are: medium of exchange, unit of account (measure of value), store of value, and standard of deferred payment.

 

• Money as a "store of value" allows wealth to be held and used later, while as a "standard of deferred payment" it facilitates credit/loan transactions across time.

 

NOTE

 

• Store of value (Option 1): Relates to holding wealth over time, not to measuring/aggregating output like GDP.

 

• Standard of deferred payments (Option 3): Relates to settling future/credit obligations, not to valuing current output.

 

• Medium of exchange (Option 4): Relates to money's use in facilitating transactions/purchases, not specifically to measuring and aggregating the value of national output.

question: In which year were the first Olympic Games held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1896.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first modern Olympic Games were held in 1896 in Athens, Greece, reviving the ancient Greek Olympic tradition. (प्रथम आधुनिक ओलंपिक खेल — एथेंस, 1896)

 

• They were organised by the International Olympic Committee (IOC), founded in 1894 on the initiative of Baron Pierre de Coubertin, regarded as the father of the modern Olympic Movement.

 

• The 1896 Games featured athletes from 14 nations competing in 43 events across 9 sports.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ancient Olympic Games were held in Olympia, Greece, starting around 776 BCE, in honour of the god Zeus.

 

• The Olympic Games are held every 4 years, an interval known as an Olympiad; the Winter Olympics were introduced separately, first held in 1924.

 

NOTE

 

• 1900 (Option 1): Paris hosted the 2nd modern Olympic Games in 1900, not the first.

 

• 1984 (Option 2): Los Angeles hosted the Olympics in 1984, nearly a century after the first modern Games.

 

• 1898 (Option 4): No Olympic Games were held in this year.

question:
Which of the given statements is/are correct with respect to NAFED?

i. NAFED is registered under the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act.

ii. It was set up with the objective of promoting Cooperative marketing of agricultural produce to benefit farmers.

iii. It was established in 1956.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only i and ii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• NAFED (National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India) is registered under the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, so Statement i is correct. (नेफेड — सहकारी विपणन संघ)

 

• NAFED was set up with the core objective of promoting cooperative marketing of agricultural produce, to benefit farmer-members by ensuring remunerative prices, so Statement ii is correct.

 

• Statement iii is incorrect: NAFED was actually established on 2 October 1958 (on Gandhi Jayanti), not in 1956.

 

• Since Statements i and ii are correct but Statement iii is incorrect, the right combination is "Only i and ii".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• NAFED is also the central nodal agency for procurement of oilseeds, pulses and cotton under Price Support Scheme (PSS), and for maintaining buffer stocks of onions and pulses.

 

• It operates under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India.

 

NOTE

 

• i, ii and iii (Option 1) and Only ii and iii (Option 3): Both incorrectly include Statement iii, which wrongly states NAFED's founding year as 1956 (actual: 1958).

 

• Only ii (Option 2): Incorrectly excludes Statement i, which is a correct fact about NAFED's registration.

question: During the 2022 Commonwealth Games held in Birmingham, how many medals did India win?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 61.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India won a total of 61 medals at the 2022 Commonwealth Games held in Birmingham, England — comprising 22 gold, 16 silver and 23 bronze medals. (2022 राष्ट्रमंडल खेल, बर्मिंघम — भारत 61 पदक)

 

• India finished 4th in the overall medal tally, behind Australia, England and Canada.

 

• Standout performances came from weightlifting, wrestling, badminton, table tennis and boxing, with Mirabai Chanu winning India's first gold of the Games in weightlifting.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2022 Commonwealth Games were the 22nd edition, held from 28 July to 8 August 2022 in Birmingham, England.

 

• The next Commonwealth Games are scheduled to be held in Glasgow, Scotland, in 2026.

 

NOTE

 

• 65, 55 and 40 (Options 1, 2 and 4): None of these match India's actual total medal count of 61 at the 2022 Birmingham Commonwealth Games.

question: Which of the following are categorised in the Right to Constitutional Remedies in the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Articles 32-35.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Right to Constitutional Remedies, one of the six Fundamental Rights guaranteed under Part III of the Indian Constitution, is covered under Articles 32 to 35. (संवैधानिक उपचारों का अधिकार — अनुच्छेद 32-35)

 

• Article 32 gives every citizen the right to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights, through writs such as habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari and quo warranto; Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called it the "heart and soul of the Constitution".

 

• Article 33 empowers Parliament to restrict/modify Fundamental Rights for armed forces, para-military and intelligence personnel; Article 34 allows restriction of rights during martial law; Article 35 empowers Parliament (not state legislatures) to make laws to give effect to certain Fundamental Rights (e.g., under Articles 16, 32, 33 and 34).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs as well, for enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for other purposes — a wider jurisdiction than Article 32.

 

• The six Fundamental Rights in Part III are: Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.

 

NOTE

 

• Articles 32-36, Articles 31-34 and Articles 33-36 (Options 2, 3 and 4): These ranges are incorrect; the Right to Constitutional Remedies is specifically Articles 32-35. (Article 31 was repealed by the 44th Amendment; Article 36 belongs to the Directive Principles chapter, Part IV, defining "the State".)

question: The target for the first commitment period of the Kyoto Protocol is to reduce emissions of how many greenhouse gases by 5.2% from 1990 levels?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kyoto Protocol, adopted in 1997 and entering into force in 2005, set a target for its first commitment period (2008-2012) to reduce emissions of six greenhouse gases by at least 5.2% below 1990 levels. (क्योटो प्रोटोकॉल — 6 ग्रीनहाउस गैसें)

 

• The six greenhouse gases covered are: Carbon dioxide (CO2), Methane (CH4), Nitrous oxide (N2O), Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), Perfluorocarbons (PFCs) and Sulphur hexafluoride (SF6).

 

• The Protocol was adopted under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) at Kyoto, Japan, and followed the principle of "Common but Differentiated Responsibilities", placing binding targets primarily on developed (Annex I) countries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A second commitment period (2013-2020) was adopted via the Doha Amendment (2012).

 

• The Kyoto Protocol was eventually succeeded by the Paris Agreement (2015), which set a broader, more inclusive global climate framework.

 

NOTE

 

• 10, 8 and 7 (Options 2, 3 and 4): These do not match the actual count; the Kyoto Protocol's first commitment period target covers exactly six greenhouse gases.
